fix: After a header like 'Flowers: tepals ...', the bearer is the noun right after the colon (tepals). The header noun only names the whole.
reason: The colour range dark reddish brown to light brown is said of the tepals, not of the whole flower. The quality and the value range are right.

target: position: upper (cells of the upper leaf)
fix: In 'upper leaf-cells ..., the basal smooth', the position word 'upper' must be kept, because the same flora contrasts it with the basal cells.
reason: Only the upper leaf cells are faintly papillose; the basal cells are said to be smooth. Without 'upper', the annotation says all leaf cells are papillose, which is false.
The branchlets are brownish or grayish brown. The two values are right, and 'approximately' stands for the '-ish'.

fix: In 'Needles ..., margin usually not inflexed', the 'margin' is a part of the needle. The bearer is the margin, not the leaf.
reason: The flora says the needle margin is not inflexed, not the whole needle. The negation and the word 'usually' are right.
The stamens are shorter than the petals; the comparison target is right.
The leaves (reduced to scales) are ± scarious.

target: glaucous (PATO_0104277), on the abaxial surface of the blade
fix: 'glaucous' must map to PATO_0104277 glaucous (a whitish waxy bloom), not to 'approximately green'. Here 'green' belongs to the adaxial side of the next clause.
reason: The statement says the blade is glaucous on its lower (abaxial) side. The annotation instead gives the blade 'about green' with no side, mixing in the next clause.

fix: For a stigma, 'capitate' or 'subcapitate' means head-shaped (FLOPO_0991097). FLOPO_0991006 capitate is only for flowers grouped in heads (an inflorescence arrangement).
reason: A subcapitate stigma is a stigma that is nearly head-shaped. It is not flowers clustered into a head.
The corolla lobes range from oblong to ligulate (strap-shaped, PATO_0002430).
The leaf blade has 8–20 teeth on each side; the count and its 'each side' position are right.
The outer sepals are ovate, and the 'outer' position is kept.

target: calyx lobe / sepal (PO_0009031), the 2 longer segments, stage: fruit
fix: In 'N calyx segments <shape>', the bearer is the segment (a calyx lobe), not the whole calyx. A count that picks out some of the segments ('2 ... longer' against '3 shorter') must be kept.
reason: Only 2 of the 5 calyx segments on the fruit are lorate (strap-shaped); the other 3 are lanceolate. The whole calyx is not strap-shaped.
The bracts are about 2.5–6 mm long. The flora's 'c.' (about) is not recorded, but the annotation is still true.
The inflorescence is few-flowered: flowers are present in the inflorescence, with the count word 'few'.

target: trichome (PO_0000282) on the stem, colour brown
fix: In '<colour> ... villous/puberulent/pubescent', the colour word belongs to the hairs, not to the part named before it.
reason: In 'Stem ± brown crisped glandular villous', 'brown' describes the villous hairs. The flora does not say the stem itself is brown.
The stamens are shorter than the petals.
The filaments are much shorter than the anthers.

fix: In '<surface> <hairy> young, glabrescent', the word 'young' (or 'when young') sets the stage and must fill the stage slot.
reason: The adaxial surface is pilose only when young and becomes glabrous later. Without the stage, the annotation says the mature surface is pilose.
The leaf blade is glabrous on its adaxial side.
The petals are much shorter than the sepals.
The calyx lobes are 0.1 cm wide; sepal stands in for the calyx lobe.
The style is about as long as the stamens (ratio 1). The flora's 'about' is not recorded, but the annotation is still true.

fix: 'glaucous' must map to PATO_0104277 glaucous, not to 'approximately green'.
reason: The plant is glaucous (covered with a waxy bloom). The flora does not call it green.
The female inflorescences are 8–15 cm, and the 'female' context is kept.

fix: After 'Staminodes 5, ...; filaments ...', the filaments belong to the staminodes, so the staminode whole must fill the whole slot.
reason: Only the staminodes' filaments are adnate to the petals. Nothing is said of the filaments of the fertile stamens.
The plant height of 1–4.5 dm is correctly converted to 10–45 cm. The second number (4–20 dm) is the width and is not part of this annotation.
'obovate-elliptic' names a shape between obovate and elliptic, so reading it as a continuum is acceptable. The bearer is the fruit.

target: trichome (PO_0000282) on the twig, colour brown
fix: In '<colour> ... villous/puberulent/pubescent', the colour word belongs to the hairs, not to the part named before it.
reason: In '± brownish puberulent', 'brownish' describes the hairs. The flora says the twig itself is pale brown, which is a different statement.
The plants are annual or perennial; both life spans are given as alternatives.
There are 3 styles, rarely 4; the count 3 with an upper extreme of 4 is right.
